q-lateinamerika-47#explanation: Because letters to Spain took months, local officials had great leeway and could formally acknowledge orders without implementing them.
q-lateinamerika-48#question: Which veneration of the Virgin Mary became a symbol of Mexico?
q-lateinamerika-48#explanation: Her veneration blended Christian and older beliefs; in 1810 Miguel Hidalgo's rebel army marched under her banner.
q-lateinamerika-49#question: About which culture did the Franciscan Bernardino de Sahagún write a major work?
q-lateinamerika-49#explanation: Sahagún learned Nahuatl and, with Indigenous informants, recorded knowledge about the religion, daily life and history of the Aztecs.
q-lateinamerika-50#question: Which artist created distinctive Baroque masterpieces in Minas Gerais in the 18th century?
q-lateinamerika-50#explanation: The sculptor and architect Aleijadinho combined European forms with his own style; his works bear witness to the wealth of the Brazilian gold rush.
q-lateinamerika-51#question: What consequence did the abolition of slavery in 1888 have for the Brazilian monarchy?
q-lateinamerika-51#choices.0: It was strengthened by the planters' gratitude
q-lateinamerika-51#choices.2: Princess Isabel was immediately crowned empress
q-lateinamerika-51#choices.3: Angry planters supported its overthrow in 1889
q-lateinamerika-51#explanation: The Lei Áurea abolished slavery without compensating the owners; the very next year the republic was proclaimed and the imperial family went into exile.
q-lateinamerika-52#question: Which regions became the centers of plantation sugar production in the colonial era?
q-lateinamerika-52#explanation: On the sugar plantations enslaved Africans processed sugarcane into raw sugar for Europe under murderous conditions.
q-mittelalter-01#question: Who was crowned emperor in Rome at Christmas in the year 800?
q-mittelalter-01#explanation: Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne emperor in St. Peter's on December 25, 800.
q-mittelalter-02#question: Which event is regarded as the beginning of the Viking Age?
q-mittelalter-02#choices.0: The raid on the monastery of Lindisfarne in 793
q-mittelalter-02#explanation: The raid on the monastery of Lindisfarne in the year 793 caused horror across Europe and marks the beginning of the Viking Age.
q-mittelalter-03#question: What did the Magna Carta of 1215 lay down?
q-mittelalter-03#choices.0: The division of the Frankish Empire
q-mittelalter-03#choices.1: The election of the pope by cardinals
q-mittelalter-03#choices.2: That the king is bound by the law and may levy no taxes without consent
q-mittelalter-03#choices.3: The founding of the University of Oxford
q-mittelalter-03#explanation: King John had to assure the barons that no one would be imprisoned without judgment and that no tax would be levied without the consent of the council.
q-mittelalter-04#question: Which empire did Mansa Musa rule, who made the pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324?
q-mittelalter-04#explanation: Mansa Musa was king of the West African Mali Empire, which controlled the gold trade across the Sahara.
q-mittelalter-05#question: Which city did Joan of Arc liberate in 1429 during the Hundred Years' War?
q-mittelalter-05#explanation: In May 1429 Joan of Arc ended the English siege of Orléans and afterward led the Dauphin to Reims for his coronation.
q-mittelalter-06#explanation: Mehmed II, called the Conqueror, took Constantinople on May 29, 1453 and made it the capital of the Ottoman Empire.
q-mittelalter-07#question: Which king waited as a penitent before the castle of Canossa in 1077 for the pope's forgiveness?
q-mittelalter-07#explanation: During the Investiture Controversy, Henry IV asked Pope Gregory VII at Canossa to release him from the excommunication the pope had imposed on him in 1076.
q-mittelalter-08#question: What did the Treaty of Verdun lay down in 843?
q-mittelalter-08#choices.0: The imperial coronation of Otto I
q-mittelalter-08#choices.1: The end of the Viking raids
q-mittelalter-08#choices.2: The division of the Frankish Empire among the grandsons of Charlemagne
q-mittelalter-08#choices.3: The founding of the Hanseatic League
q-mittelalter-08#explanation: At Verdun, Charles the Bald, Louis the German and Lothair I divided the Frankish Empire into a western, an eastern and a middle kingdom.
q-mittelalter-09#question: Which emperor had the Hagia Sophia built in Constantinople between 532 and 537?
q-mittelalter-09#explanation: Justinian I had the Hagia Sophia rebuilt after the Nika revolt and consecrated it in 537; for almost a thousand years it was the largest church in the world.
q-mittelalter-10#question: Whom did Otto I defeat on the Lechfeld near Augsburg in the year 955?
q-mittelalter-10#explanation: In 955 Otto I defeated the Hungarian mounted warriors who had been plundering central Europe for decades, and he was crowned emperor in 962.
q-mittelalter-11#question: Which ruler turned the city-state of Cusco into the Inca Empire from about 1438 onward?
q-mittelalter-11#explanation: Pachacuti defeated the Chanka, expanded Cusco into a capital and founded the empire of Tawantinsuyu; Atahualpa was the last Inca before the Spanish conquest.
q-mittelalter-12#question: What did the stone city of Great Zimbabwe in southern Africa live on above all between the 13th and 15th centuries?
q-mittelalter-12#choices.0: On the salt trade across the Sahara
q-mittelalter-12#choices.1: On the silk trade with Byzantium
q-mittelalter-12#choices.2: On the gold and ivory trade with the Swahili Coast
q-mittelalter-12#choices.3: On the fur trade with Novgorod
q-mittelalter-12#explanation: The rulers of Great Zimbabwe controlled gold deposits and herds of cattle and traded through ports such as Kilwa and Sofala as far as India and China.
q-mittelalter-13#question: Why was it significant that the Frankish king Clovis adopted the Catholic rather than the Arian creed?
q-mittelalter-13#choices.0: It won him the support of the Church and the Roman population
q-mittelalter-13#choices.1: The pope rewarded him with the imperial crown
q-mittelalter-13#choices.2: It made him co-emperor of the Eastern Roman Empire
q-mittelalter-13#choices.3: It ended all his wars with the Visigoths
q-mittelalter-13#explanation: Unlike most Germanic kings, Clovis chose the Catholic faith at Reims around 498; even so, he defeated the Arian Visigoths in 507.
q-mittelalter-14#question: Which father of monasticism founded the monastery of Monte Cassino around 529 and wrote a rule adopted by almost all monasteries in the West?
q-mittelalter-14#explanation: The Rule of Benedict divided the monks' day between prayer, reading and manual labour and demanded moderation and obedience to the abbot.
q-mittelalter-15#question: Who designed the Hagia Sophia, with its seemingly floating dome, for Emperor Justinian?
q-mittelalter-15#choices.3: Anthemius of Tralles and Isidore of Miletus
q-mittelalter-15#explanation: The two mathematicians completed the building in just five years; for almost a thousand years afterwards Hagia Sophia was the largest church in Christendom.
q-mittelalter-16#question: Which legal code did Emperor Justinian have compiled that still shapes Europe's legal systems today?
q-mittelalter-16#explanation: A commission of jurists under Tribonian compiled the whole of Roman law; from the 11th century onward it was studied anew in Bologna.
q-mittelalter-17#question: Which empress persuaded Justinian not to flee Constantinople during the Nika riots of 532?
q-mittelalter-17#explanation: According to Procopius, Theodora declared that royal purple makes a fine burial shroud; the former actress later also pushed through laws in favour of women.
q-mittelalter-18#question: In which city is the famous mosaic portrait of Empress Theodora located?
q-mittelalter-18#explanation: The mosaic adorns the church of San Vitale in Ravenna, which Justinian had reconquered in his war against the Ostrogoths.
q-mittelalter-19#question: Which region in northern France is named after the Norsemen who settled there?
q-mittelalter-19#explanation: The Vikings founded Normandy; their descendants, the Normans, conquered England in 1066 under Duke William.
q-mittelalter-20#question: In which city did Charlemagne build his palace with a chapel that still stands today?
q-mittelalter-20#explanation: The Palatine Chapel is now part of Aachen Cathedral, where Charlemagne was buried and where many German kings were later crowned.
q-mittelalter-21#question: Which Anglo-Saxon scholar did Charlemagne bring to his court to lead his educational reform?
q-mittelalter-21#explanation: Alcuin of York headed the palace school; thanks to Charlemagne's educational reform, many ancient texts have survived.
q-mittelalter-22#choices.0: A clear, legible script developed under Charlemagne
q-mittelalter-22#choices.2: An order of prayer for monasteries
q-mittelalter-22#explanation: This clear lower-case script is part of the Carolingian Renaissance and the model for our lower-case letters today.
q-mittelalter-23#question: What are the Oaths of Strasbourg of 842?
q-mittelalter-23#choices.0: The oath of loyalty of the subjugated Saxons to Charlemagne
q-mittelalter-23#choices.1: A peace treaty between the Franks and the Hungarians
q-mittelalter-23#choices.2: An alliance sworn by Charles the Bald and Louis the German in two vernacular languages
q-mittelalter-23#choices.3: Otto I's coronation oath in Aachen
q-mittelalter-23#explanation: Sworn in Old French and Old High German, the oaths are regarded as the oldest records of both languages; the Treaty of Verdun followed a year later.
q-mittelalter-24#question: Which archbishopric did Otto the Great found in 968 as a base for the mission to the Slavs?
q-mittelalter-24#explanation: Magdeburg was Otto's favourite residence; he is also buried in Magdeburg Cathedral.
q-mittelalter-25#question: Which grand prince of Kievan Rus was baptized in 988 and made Orthodox Christianity the religion of his realm?
q-mittelalter-25#explanation: Vladimir married Anna, the sister of the Byzantine emperor Basil II; along with the faith, the Cyrillic script and icon painting came to Rus.
q-mittelalter-26#question: In which year did the Normans under Duke William conquer England?
q-mittelalter-26#explanation: William won at Hastings on 14 October 1066 and had himself crowned at Westminster on Christmas Day.
q-mittelalter-27#question: What did William the Conqueror have recorded in the Domesday Book in 1086?
q-mittelalter-27#choices.0: The landholdings and dues of the entire kingdom
q-mittelalter-27#choices.1: The laws of the Anglo-Saxon kings
q-mittelalter-27#choices.2: The names of all those killed at Hastings
q-mittelalter-27#choices.3: The family tree of the Norman ruling house
q-mittelalter-27#explanation: The Domesday Book was a nationwide survey for tax purposes and reflects the tight administration the Normans brought to England.
q-mittelalter-28#question: Which work of art tells the story of the Norman conquest of England on some 70 metres of cloth?
q-mittelalter-28#explanation: The embroidered linen strip depicts the events up to the Battle of Hastings, in which the Anglo-Saxon king Harold was killed.
q-mittelalter-29#question: Which agreement ended the Investiture Controversy in 1122?
q-mittelalter-29#explanation: The Concordat of Worms separated the spiritual investiture of bishops with ring and staff from their secular investiture by the king.
q-mittelalter-30#question: Which of these High Middle Ages events happened first?
q-mittelalter-30#choices.0: The capture of Jerusalem in the First Crusade
q-mittelalter-30#choices.3: The beginning of Gothic architecture at Saint-Denis
q-mittelalter-30#explanation: Henry IV went to Canossa in 1077; Jerusalem fell in 1099, the Concordat of Worms followed in 1122, and the rebuilding of Saint-Denis began in 1140.
q-mittelalter-31#question: Which university is regarded as the oldest in Europe?
q-mittelalter-31#explanation: In Bologna, students of Roman law formed associations around 1088; Paris and Oxford followed in the 12th century.
q-mittelalter-32#question: With which scholar did Thomas Aquinas study in Cologne and Paris?
q-mittelalter-32#explanation: Like Thomas, Albertus Magnus was a Dominican and studied Aristotle intensively; Thomas then brought scholasticism to its peak.
q-mittelalter-33#question: Which pope called for the First Crusade at the Council of Clermont in 1095?
q-mittelalter-33#explanation: Urban II wanted to help the Byzantine Christians and free the holy sites; the crusaders captured Jerusalem in 1099.
q-mittelalter-34#question: How did Emperor Frederick II regain Jerusalem for the Christians on his crusade of 1228/29?
q-mittelalter-34#choices.0: Through a treaty with Sultan al-Kamil
q-mittelalter-34#choices.1: By storming the city after a long siege
q-mittelalter-34#choices.3: Through an alliance with the Mongols
q-mittelalter-34#explanation: Frederick obtained Jerusalem without a battle, even though the pope had excommunicated him; contemporaries called him the Wonder of the World.
q-mittelalter-35#question: What is the name of the architectural style with pointed arches, rib vaults and large stained-glass windows that emerged in France around 1140?
q-mittelalter-35#explanation: Cathedrals such as Chartres, Reims and Cologne are masterpieces of the Gothic style; the name was coined disparagingly only in the Renaissance.
q-mittelalter-36#question: In which church did Abbot Suger begin the rebuilding in 1140 that is regarded as the beginning of Gothic architecture?
q-mittelalter-36#explanation: The abbey church of Saint-Denis was the burial place of the French kings; for Suger, the light streaming in was an image of God.
q-mittelalter-37#question: Which English king was forced to seal Magna Carta in 1215?
q-mittelalter-37#explanation: John had turned the nobility against him through lost wars in France and heavy taxes; he sealed the charter in the meadow at Runnymede.
q-mittelalter-38#question: To which two kings was Eleanor of Aquitaine married, one after the other?
q-mittelalter-38#choices.0: Philip II of France and Richard the Lionheart
q-mittelalter-38#choices.1: Louis IX of France and John Lackland
q-mittelalter-38#choices.2: Louis VII of France and Henry II of England
q-mittelalter-38#choices.3: Frederick Barbarossa and Henry II of England
q-mittelalter-38#explanation: Eleanor accompanied Louis VII on the Second Crusade and married Henry Plantagenet in 1152; Richard the Lionheart and John Lackland were her sons.
q-mittelalter-39#question: Which abbess wrote the visionary book Scivias, composed sacred songs and was made a Doctor of the Church in 2012?
q-mittelalter-39#explanation: Around 1150 Hildegard founded the convent of Rupertsberg near Bingen, wrote about healing plants and corresponded with Frederick Barbarossa.
q-mittelalter-40#question: Which weapon gave the English their victories at Crécy, Poitiers and Agincourt in the Hundred Years' War?
q-mittelalter-40#explanation: English longbowmen shot faster and farther than the crossbowmen of their opponents and wore down the French armies of knights.
q-mittelalter-41#question: Which town remained England's only possession on the French mainland after the end of the Hundred Years' War in 1453?
q-mittelalter-41#explanation: After the defeat at Castillon in 1453, Bordeaux was lost as well; Calais remained English until 1558.
q-mittelalter-42#question: In which city was Joan of Arc burned as a heretic in 1431?
q-mittelalter-42#explanation: Joan had been captured by the Burgundians and handed over to the English; the verdict was overturned in 1456.
q-mittelalter-43#question: Which pathogen caused the Black Death?
q-mittelalter-43#explanation: The plague bacterium was transmitted mainly by rat fleas; from 1347 onward about a third of Europe's population died.
q-mittelalter-44#question: What economic consequence did the Black Death have in Europe?
q-mittelalter-44#choices.1: Falling wages due to mass unemployment
q-mittelalter-44#choices.2: A labour shortage and rising wages
q-mittelalter-44#choices.3: A surplus of labour in the countryside
q-mittelalter-44#explanation: Because so many people died, survivors gained bargaining power; attempts to freeze wages contributed, for example, to the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381.
q-mittelalter-45#question: In which Russian city did the Hanseatic League maintain one of its major trading offices (Kontore)?
q-mittelalter-45#explanation: Besides the Peterhof in Novgorod, the Hanseatic League had Kontore in London, Bruges and Bergen, through which it dominated trade in the North Sea and Baltic.
q-mittelalter-46#question: Which king did the Hanseatic League force to make far-reaching concessions in the Peace of Stralsund in 1370?
q-mittelalter-46#explanation: After a war against Valdemar IV, the Peace of Stralsund secured trade privileges for the Hanseatic League and, for a time, castles on the Øresund.
q-mittelalter-47#question: Which type of ship was the typical merchant vessel of the Hanseatic League?
q-mittelalter-47#explanation: The broad-bellied cog with a single mast and square sail could carry large cargoes of grain, timber, salt and herring across the North Sea and Baltic.
q-mittelalter-48#question: Who led the rebellious peasants and craftsmen of England to London in 1381?
q-mittelalter-48#explanation: Wat Tyler was killed during negotiations with the young King Richard II, after which the revolt was crushed.
q-mittelalter-49#question: According to the medieval doctrine of the three orders, which estate was responsible for praying?
q-mittelalter-49#explanation: According to the doctrine of the time, the clergy prayed, the nobility fought and the peasants worked; revolts such as that of 1381 challenged this order.
q-mittelalter-50#question: In the feudal system, what did a vassal owe his lord in return for the fief he received?
q-mittelalter-50#choices.1: A fixed rent in silver coins
q-mittelalter-50#choices.2: The construction of a castle for the lord
q-mittelalter-50#explanation: Through the feudal system, a chain of personal dependencies arose from the king through dukes and counts down to the simple knight.
q-mittelalter-51#question: From which Burgundian monastery did a great reform movement of monasticism spread in the 10th and 11th centuries?
q-mittelalter-51#explanation: Founded in 910, the abbey of Cluny was subject directly to the pope; its reform spread through hundreds of dependent monasteries across Europe.
q-mittelalter-52#question: Which of these events happened first?
q-mittelalter-52#explanation: The Treaty of Verdun dates from 843; Hastings followed in 1066, Magna Carta in 1215 and the Black Death from 1347.
q-osmanisches-reich-01#question: In which year did the Ottomans conquer Constantinople?
q-osmanisches-reich-01#explanation: Sultan Mehmed II conquered Constantinople on 29 May 1453 and made the city, as Istanbul, his capital.
q-osmanisches-reich-02#question: Which sultan bore the epithet "the Magnificent" and besieged Vienna in 1529?
q-osmanisches-reich-02#explanation: Suleiman I, called "the Magnificent" in Europe, reigned from 1520 to 1566 and besieged Vienna in vain in 1529.
q-osmanisches-reich-03#question: What was the name of the sultans' standing infantry corps that Mahmud II dissolved in 1826?
q-osmanisches-reich-03#explanation: The Janissaries revolted against a new army in 1826 and were then dissolved by Mahmud II.
q-osmanisches-reich-04#question: Which city did Orhan conquer in 1326 and make the first capital of the Ottomans?
q-osmanisches-reich-04#explanation: Orhan conquered Byzantine Bursa in 1326; only later did Edirne and then Istanbul become the capital.
q-osmanisches-reich-05#question: Who defeated Sultan Bayezid I at the Battle of Ankara in 1402?
q-osmanisches-reich-05#explanation: Timur defeated and captured Bayezid I near Ankara; an eleven-year struggle for the throne among the Ottomans followed.
q-osmanisches-reich-06#question: Which country did Selim I conquer in 1517, ending the rule of the Mamluks there?
q-osmanisches-reich-06#explanation: After the victory at Ridaniya outside Cairo in 1517, Egypt became an Ottoman province.
q-osmanisches-reich-07#question: Who founded the first press for books in Ottoman Turkish in 1727?
q-osmanisches-reich-07#explanation: İbrahim Müteferrika received permission to print in 1727; his first book appeared in 1729.
q-osmanisches-reich-08#question: Which master builder erected the Süleymaniye Mosque in Istanbul?
q-osmanisches-reich-08#explanation: The court architect Sinan built the Süleymaniye Mosque from 1550 to 1557.
q-osmanisches-reich-09#question: What did the Edict of Gülhane of 1839 promise, among other things?
q-osmanisches-reich-09#choices.0: Equality of all subjects before the law regardless of religion
q-osmanisches-reich-09#choices.2: The introduction of the Latin alphabet
q-osmanisches-reich-09#choices.3: The declaration of war on Russia
q-osmanisches-reich-09#explanation: The edict opened the Tanzimat reforms and promised security of life and property as well as legal equality for Muslims and non-Muslims.
q-osmanisches-reich-10#question: In which peace treaty of 1699 did the Ottoman Empire cede Hungary to the Habsburgs?
q-osmanisches-reich-10#explanation: In the Treaty of Karlowitz in 1699 the Habsburgs received almost all of Hungary and Transylvania.
q-osmanisches-reich-11#question: Which provision did the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca of 1774 contain?
q-osmanisches-reich-11#choices.1: The cession of Egypt to France
q-osmanisches-reich-11#choices.2: The independence of the Crimean Khanate from the Ottomans
q-osmanisches-reich-11#choices.3: The return of Hungary to the Ottomans
q-osmanisches-reich-11#explanation: The Crimean Khanate became independent in 1774 and was annexed by Russia in 1783.
q-osmanisches-reich-12#question: Which sultan's mother led the regency for Murad IV from 1623 and later for her grandson Mehmed IV?
q-osmanisches-reich-12#explanation: As valide sultan, Kösem Sultan shaped politics for almost three decades and was murdered in 1651.
q-osmanisches-reich-13#question: Who is the Ottoman Empire named after?
q-osmanisches-reich-13#choices.1: Osman I, the founder of the dynasty
q-osmanisches-reich-13#choices.2: Murad I, the victor of Kosovo
q-osmanisches-reich-13#choices.3: Bayezid I, the opponent of Timur
q-osmanisches-reich-13#explanation: Osman I ruled a small principality near Söğüt in north-western Anatolia around 1300. The rulers and their empire called themselves "Ottomans" (Osmanlı) after him.
q-osmanisches-reich-14#question: Which Balkan city, formerly Adrianople, did the Ottomans make their new capital after Bursa?
q-osmanisches-reich-14#explanation: Adrianople fell to the Ottomans in the 1360s and, as Edirne, served as their capital until Mehmed II conquered Constantinople in 1453. Sinan later built the Selimiye Mosque there.
q-osmanisches-reich-15#question: Which Serbian prince led the army against Sultan Murad I at Kosovo Polje in 1389?
q-osmanisches-reich-15#explanation: Prince Lazar was captured in the battle and executed; Murad I was killed as well. In Serbian memory the battle became a myth that still resonates today.
q-osmanisches-reich-16#question: Who was the last Byzantine emperor, killed defending Constantinople in 1453?
q-osmanisches-reich-16#explanation: Constantine XI fell on 29 May 1453 when Ottoman troops breached the walls with the help of enormous cannons. This ended the Eastern Roman Empire after more than a thousand years.
q-osmanisches-reich-17#question: What epithet did Mehmed II receive after conquering Constantinople?
q-osmanisches-reich-17#explanation: Mehmed II took Constantinople at the age of 21 and was called Fatih, "the Conqueror". He resettled Muslims, Christians and Jews in the depopulated city.
q-osmanisches-reich-18#question: Which church did Mehmed II convert into a mosque after conquering Constantinople?
q-osmanisches-reich-18#choices.3: The Church of the Holy Sepulchre
q-osmanisches-reich-18#explanation: The Hagia Sophia, built in the 6th century under Justinian, became a mosque in 1453. Ottoman architects such as Sinan later took its dome as their model.
q-osmanisches-reich-19#question: Which palace in Istanbul was the sultans' seat of government for almost 400 years?
q-osmanisches-reich-19#explanation: Mehmed II had Topkapı Palace built around 1459 above the Bosporus and the Golden Horn. Only in 1856 did the court move to Dolmabahçe Palace; Topkapı has been a museum since 1924.
q-osmanisches-reich-20#question: Which empire did Selim I fight at the Battle of Chaldiran in 1514?
q-osmanisches-reich-20#explanation: At Chaldiran Selim I defeated Shah Ismail I, above all thanks to his artillery and Janissaries. The border between the Sunni Ottoman Empire and Shiite Persia shaped the region for centuries.
q-osmanisches-reich-21#question: Which Hungarian city did the Ottomans capture in 1541, turning central Hungary into a province for 150 years?
q-osmanisches-reich-21#explanation: With the capture of Buda in 1541, central Hungary became an Ottoman province. Only in the Great Turkish War after 1683 did the Habsburgs reconquer the region.
q-osmanisches-reich-22#question: Who led the defence of Vienna against Suleiman's army in 1529?
q-osmanisches-reich-22#explanation: The small garrison under Count Niklas Salm repelled mines and assaults until rain and the approaching winter forced the Ottomans to withdraw in mid-October. Starhemberg defended Vienna only in 1683.
q-osmanisches-reich-23#question: Which future writer was wounded at the naval Battle of Lepanto in 1571?
q-osmanisches-reich-23#explanation: Cervantes fought for the Holy League and lost the use of his left hand. Despite the defeat, the Ottomans rebuilt their fleet within a year.
q-osmanisches-reich-24#question: Which sultan had the coffeehouses of Istanbul closed in 1633?
q-osmanisches-reich-24#explanation: Religious scholars and sultans distrusted coffeehouses as places of criticism. The first ones had been opened around 1555 by two men from Aleppo and Damascus.
q-osmanisches-reich-25#question: What title did the mother of the reigning sultan, one of the most powerful people at court, hold?
q-osmanisches-reich-25#explanation: The Valide Sultan headed the harem and often wielded great political influence. Haseki Sultan, by contrast, was the title of the sultan's favoured consort.
q-osmanisches-reich-26#question: What do historians call the period in the 17th century when palace women such as Kösem held great political power?
q-osmanisches-reich-26#explanation: Sultan mothers such as Kösem acted as regents for underage sultans. The Tulip Era came later, from 1718 to 1730.
q-osmanisches-reich-27#question: What is the ten-volume work in which Evliya Çelebi described his decades of travel?
q-osmanisches-reich-27#explanation: The Seyahatname, the "Book of Travels", mixes precise observations about cities, languages and food with anecdotes and exaggerations. It is one of the most important sources on everyday life in the 17th century.
q-osmanisches-reich-28#question: Under which sultan did Istanbul experience the so-called Tulip Era (1718–1730)?
q-osmanisches-reich-28#explanation: Ahmed III and his grand vizier Damat İbrahim Pasha relied on diplomacy, gardens and festivities. In 1730 the revolt of Patrona Halil toppled them both.
q-osmanisches-reich-29#question: Which book was the first to appear from İbrahim Müteferrika's press in 1729?
q-osmanisches-reich-29#explanation: Religious texts were excluded from the printing permit, so Müteferrika printed secular works. By 1742 he had published 17 books, including histories and maps.
q-osmanisches-reich-30#question: Which headgear did Mahmud II introduce for officials in place of the turban?
q-osmanisches-reich-30#explanation: With this dress reform Mahmud II wanted to create a modern, uniform civil service. He also founded ministries and, in 1831, the first official newspaper.
q-osmanisches-reich-31#question: What did the Ottoman government call "the Auspicious Incident"?
q-osmanisches-reich-31#choices.2: The proclamation of the constitution in 1876
q-osmanisches-reich-31#choices.3: The destruction of the Janissaries in 1826
q-osmanisches-reich-31#explanation: In June 1826 Mahmud II had the barracks of the rebelling Janissaries shelled and the corps dissolved. This cleared the way for a modern army.
q-osmanisches-reich-32#question: Which Sufi order was closely tied to the Janissaries and banned together with them in 1826?
q-osmanisches-reich-32#explanation: The Bektashi shaped the popular piety of the Janissaries. The Mevlevi order with its dervishes, by contrast, survived and was patronised by sultans such as Selim III.
q-osmanisches-reich-33#question: Under which sultan was the Edict of Gülhane proclaimed in 1839?
q-osmanisches-reich-33#explanation: A few months after Mahmud II's death, foreign minister Mustafa Reşid Pasha read out the edict of the young Abdülmecid I. It marked the start of the Tanzimat.
q-osmanisches-reich-34#question: Who set new standards of nursing at the military hospital in Scutari (Üsküdar) during the Crimean War?
q-osmanisches-reich-34#explanation: In the Crimean War disease killed more soldiers than weapons did. Florence Nightingale improved hygiene and care at the hospital opposite Istanbul and became a model for modern nursing.
q-osmanisches-reich-35#question: Which country did the Ottoman Empire fight in the Crimean War of 1853–1856?
q-osmanisches-reich-35#explanation: Britain and France entered the war on the Ottoman side to stop Russia's advance towards the Straits. The Peace of Paris in 1856 neutralised the Black Sea.
q-osmanisches-reich-36#question: What mocking name did European diplomats give the Ottoman Empire in the 19th century?
q-osmanisches-reich-36#explanation: The name alluded to the empire's military defeats, territorial losses and debts. In 1875 the state did indeed go bankrupt.
q-osmanisches-reich-37#question: Which grand vizier is regarded as the father of the first Ottoman constitution of 1876?
q-osmanisches-reich-37#explanation: Midhat Pasha shaped the constitution, the Kanun-ı Esasi, but was exiled by Abdülhamid II as early as February 1877. He was murdered in Taif in 1884.
q-osmanisches-reich-38#question: Which cities did the Hejaz Railway connect from 1908?
q-osmanisches-reich-38#explanation: The railway was largely financed by donations from Muslims worldwide and cut the pilgrimage from weeks to days. The planned extension to Mecca was never built.
q-osmanisches-reich-39#question: Which state did not become independent at the Congress of Berlin in 1878 but only an autonomous principality?
q-osmanisches-reich-39#explanation: The congress, chaired by Bismarck, shrank the large Bulgaria envisaged in the Treaty of San Stefano. Serbia, Montenegro and Romania became independent; Bulgaria only did so in 1908.
q-osmanisches-reich-40#question: In which naval battle did British, French and Russian ships destroy the Ottoman-Egyptian fleet in 1827?
q-osmanisches-reich-40#explanation: The victory at Navarino decided the Greek War of Independence. In 1830 Greece was recognised as the first independent state on Ottoman soil in Europe.
